## Natural history notes

A small graylet moth characterized by gray to brownish forewings marked with small yellowish spots or patches and subtle darker lines that help it blend into bark and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of woody plants and contribute to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
